about: Where to get your own data out of common platforms (GDPR Article 15 access and Article 20 portability), which file in the export matters, and what to look at in Seebra. The links were checked on 2026-11-15; menu paths and file names inside exports change often and several sit behind a login, so follow the link and look for 'Download your data'. Tell us when one has moved.

exports.what: Every play since the account opened: track, artist, album, when, how long, skipped, shuffle, platform
exports.steps: Privacy settings → Download your data → tick 'Extended streaming history' → Request; confirm the email
exports.ideas: Listening clock (hour × weekday), artists over the years, skip rate, discovery vs repeat
exports.caveat: The faster 'Account data' export has only the last year (StreamingHistory_music_*.json, fewer fields).

exports.what: Scrobbles from every player you connected, with timestamps
exports.steps: No export needed: the API reads any public profile by user name
exports.ideas: The same listening clock, live, across services
exports.caveat: Only what was scrobbled; an API key (free) is needed.

exports.what: Play activity: song, container, play duration, end reason
exports.steps: Sign in → Request a copy of your data → Apple Media Services information
exports.ideas: Listening clock, finished vs skipped plays
exports.caveat: Many columns, inconsistent between years.

exports.what: Places you visited and trips between them (walking, driving, transit)
exports.steps: On the phone: Settings → Location → Location services → Timeline → Export Timeline data (iPhone: Google Maps → your profile → Settings → Personal content → Export Timeline data)
exports.ideas: Map of visits, time at home/work, distance by mode per month, new places per year
exports.caveat: Since 2024 Timeline lives on the phone, not in Takeout; older history may be gone if it wasn't moved.

exports.what: YouTube watch and search history, Chrome history, Maps saved places, Fitbit, Gmail metadata and 50+ more products
exports.steps: Deselect all → pick the products → choose JSON where offered → Create export
exports.ideas: YouTube watching by hour and channel, search themes over the years
exports.caveat: Pick JSON for YouTube history: HTML is the default and hard to read.

exports.what: Steps, heart rate, sleep, workouts, weight and everything apps write to Health
exports.steps: Health app → your picture (top right) → Export All Health Data
exports.ideas: Steps and resting heart rate by week, sleep against workouts, a year as a calendar heatmap
exports.caveat: export.xml is large (often 0.5–2 GB) and needs an XML reader; Seebra doesn't read it yet.

exports.what: Every activity with date, type, distance, time, elevation, and the GPS tracks
exports.steps: Settings → My Account → Download or Delete Your Account → Get started → Request your archive
exports.ideas: Distance per week by sport, pace over the years, every route on one map
exports.caveat: Tracks are GPX or gzipped FIT files; activities.csv alone is enough to start.

exports.what: Activities, sleep, stress, heart rate, body battery
exports.steps: Account → Data Management → Export Your Data → Request Data Export
exports.ideas: Training load, sleep and stress across seasons
exports.caveat: Deeply nested folders; one activity per FIT file.

exports.what: Every title a profile watched, with the date
exports.steps: Profile → Account → Profiles → Viewing activity → Download all (at the bottom). The full account archive is at netflix.com/account/getmyinfo
exports.ideas: Binges (episodes per day), series vs films, watching by weekday
exports.caveat: Titles only, with the series and episode in one string; dates use your locale's format.

exports.what: Your shelves: books, authors, ratings, dates read, pages
exports.steps: My Books → Import and export → Export Library
exports.ideas: Books and pages per year, your ratings against the average, authors read most
exports.caveat: Date Read is empty for books marked read without a date.

exports.what: Orders with items, prices, dates and addresses; Kindle reading sessions; Alexa
exports.steps: Account → Request your data → Your Orders (or All your data) → Submit; confirm the email
exports.ideas: Spending per month and category, the most repeated orders
exports.caveat: Each country's Amazon is a separate account (amazon.de, amazon.se).

exports.what: Transactions: date, text, amount, balance
exports.steps: Internet bank → the account → transactions → choose the period → Export (CSV or Excel)
exports.ideas: Spending by category and month, recurring payments (subscriptions), balance over the year
exports.caveat: Every bank writes its own columns, decimal commas and date formats; categories come from the transaction text.

exports.what: Posts, likes, comments, followers, messages, ads interests, login history
exports.steps: Accounts Center → Your information and permissions → Download your information → Download or transfer → choose JSON
exports.ideas: Followers gained over time, who you message most, what advertisers think you like
exports.caveat: Choose JSON, not HTML. Text in Meta's JSON is mis-encoded (UTF-8 read as Latin-1): å, ä, ö come out garbled until fixed.

exports.what: Posts, reactions, friends, messages, events, off-Facebook activity
exports.steps: Accounts Center → Your information and permissions → Download your information → choose JSON
exports.ideas: Friends added per year, activity over a decade, which companies share data about you
exports.caveat: Same text encoding problem as Instagram.

exports.what: Posts, likes, followers, DMs, ad data
exports.steps: Settings → Your account → Download an archive of your data → verify → Request archive
exports.ideas: Posting rhythm, replies vs posts, words over the years
exports.caveat: Files are JavaScript (window.YTD.tweets.part0 = [...]): strip the prefix to get JSON.

exports.what: Connections with company, position and date connected; messages; positions
exports.steps: Settings → Data privacy → Get a copy of your data → pick Connections (fast) or the larger archive
exports.ideas: Your network by company and year connected
exports.caveat: Connections.csv starts with a few lines of notes before the header; emails are often blank.

exports.what: One chat's messages with sender and time
exports.steps: Open the chat → contact or group name → Export chat → Without media
exports.ideas: Who writes when, reply times, a conversation's rhythm over years
exports.caveat: The line format depends on the phone's language and date settings. Other people's messages are theirs too: keep it to yourself.

exports.what: Games owned, playtime, purchases, store activity
exports.steps: Help → My Account → Data related to your Steam account
exports.ideas: Playtime per game and genre, the never-played pile
exports.caveat: Playtime per game is easier through the Web API (GetOwnedGames, needs a free key and a public profile).

exports.what: Every game you played, with moves, clocks, openings and ratings
exports.steps: No export needed: the API streams any player's games by user name
exports.ideas: Rating over time, openings that win, how time trouble ends games
exports.caveat: Large histories stream slowly; ask for one year at a time.

exports.what: Repositories, issues, pull requests, comments, events
exports.steps: Settings → Account → Export account data (or use the API live)
exports.ideas: Commits by hour, languages over the years, collaborators
exports.caveat: The public events API covers only 90 days; the archive covers everything.

exports.what: Trips with time, product, distance, fare, pickup and drop-off places
exports.steps: Privacy Center → Download your data
exports.ideas: Trips and spend per month, the routes you ride most

exports.what: Hourly electricity use (and, with a contract, the price you paid)
exports.steps: Grid company's My pages → Consumption → export hourly values (in Sweden e.g. Ellevio, Vattenfall Eldistribution, E.ON Energidistribution)
exports.ideas: Use by hour and season against outdoor temperature (SMHI) and spot price (Nord Pool)
exports.caveat: Hourly values; quarter-hour from late 2025 in the Nordics.
